question: What is the primary goal of writing a formal research report in nursing?

options.D: Communicating evidence-based findings to improve practice

explanation: Research reports translate clinical investigations into accessible data that guide bedside care and improve patient outcomes. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why must a nursing research report avoid overly ornate or literary writing styles?

options.A: Patients need to read the raw reports easily
options.B: Clarity and precision are needed for clinical application
options.C: Complex words automatically invalidate statistical data
options.D: Scientific journals strictly prohibit descriptive adjectives

explanation: Clinical readers need unambiguous facts to safely apply findings in patient care settings. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h1)

question: What do the letters in the standard IMRAD format stand for?
explanation: IMRAD is the universally accepted structural framework for organizing empirical research papers. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why do scholarly journals require a standardized structural format for research reports?

options.A: It prevents authors from writing overly long articles
options.B: It allows readers to locate specific information quickly
options.C: It eliminates the need for peer review panels

explanation: Standardized sections help busy clinicians find methodology, results, or conclusions without reading the entire document. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h2)

question: When is the abstract of a research report typically written?

options.B: Before selecting the methodology and data tools
options.C: During the initial formulation of the title page
options.D: After the entire study and report are completed

explanation: Writing the abstract last ensures it accurately summarizes all completed sections of the report. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the introduction section in a research report?

options.A: Providing a detailed breakdown of raw statistical data
options.D: Establishing the research gap and study objectives

explanation: The introduction builds the rationale for the study and clearly defines what the research aims to achieve. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of a literature review in a research report?

options.A: Replacing the need for a primary methodology section
options.B: Proving the researcher's personal opinions are correct
options.C: Synthesizing existing knowledge and identifying gaps
options.D: Listing every published book in the hospital library

explanation: A literature review connects past findings to the current study and justifies why new research is needed. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why must the methodology section contain extensive, precise details about the study design?

options.B: To hide potential flaws in statistical analysis
options.C: To increase the total word count of the document
options.D: To allow other researchers to replicate the study

explanation: Replicability is a core pillar of scientific research, requiring clear documentation of every step taken. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h4)

question: How should findings be presented in the results section of a research report?

options.A: Alongside emotional commentary from the author
options.B: Through lengthy paragraphs without any tables
options.C: By hiding any unexpected or negative outcomes
options.D: Objectively without personal interpretation or bias

explanation: The results section strictly reports what the data shows, leaving interpretations for the discussion section. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is a common error researchers make when using tables and graphs in the results section?

options.A: Placing all visual elements in the preliminary pages
options.B: Using too many numbers in the statistical summaries
options.C: Duplicating the exact text data in the visual table
options.D: Failing to include decorative borders around images

explanation: Tables and graphs should summarize and highlight trends, rather than repeating every single sentence written in the narrative. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h5)

question: In which section of a research report should the author interpret the clinical meaning of the findings?
explanation: The discussion section is where researchers explain the significance of their results and connect them back to clinical practice. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important to include study limitations in the discussion section?

options.A: It eliminates the need for future investigations
options.B: It proves the research had zero methodological errors
options.C: It guarantees immediate publication in a journal
options.D: It demonstrates scientific integrity and transparency

explanation: Acknowledging limitations shows the author understands the boundaries and potential weaknesses of their study. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable way to maintain academic integrity when writing a report?

options.A: Paraphrasing external ideas while adding correct citations
options.B: Citing the original authors properly within the text
options.C: Using approved referencing styles like APA or Vancouver
options.D: Copying paragraphs directly without quotation marks or citations

explanation: Taking another person's words or ideas without proper credit constitutes plagiarism, which is a serious ethical breach. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why must every in-text citation match the reference list at the end of the report?

options.A: To prevent the computer software from crashing
options.B: To meet the minimum word count required for school
options.C: To allow readers to verify the original sources easily
options.D: To hide the personal opinions of the lead author

explanation: Exact matching between citations and references ensures transparency and enables readers to trace the evidence. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of the peer review process in research dissemination?

options.A: Providing constructive feedback to improve report quality
options.B: Delaying publication to discourage young researchers
options.C: Checking the personal financial records of the authors
options.D: Eliminating all future need for clinical data collection

explanation: Independent reviewers evaluate the manuscript to ensure methodological soundness and clarity before publication. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h8)

question: Why is the final dissemination of research findings crucial for the nursing profession?

options.A: It reduces the need for basic nursing education
options.B: It translates new evidence into improved clinical practice
options.C: It increases the personal salary of hospital managers
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about care

explanation: Sharing findings ensures that discoveries made in research directly benefit patient outcomes at the bedside. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h8)
